chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id informed me, from Fadalah, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about one who does not recite Fatihat al-Kitab in his salat; he said: There is no salat for him except with its recitation, whether aloud or quietly.
I said: Which of the two is more beloved to you, if he is fearful or in haste: that he recite a surah or Fatihat al-Kitab? He said: Fatihat al-Kitab.

key_terms.إِخْفَاتٍ: silent or subdued recitation in prayer
key_terms.خَائِفًا: being in a state of fear
key_terms.سُورَةً: an additional surah recited after Fatihat al-Kitab
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat, the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: Surat al-Hamd, whose recitation is required in the prayer
key_terms.لَا صَلَاةَ لَهُ: an expression indicating the invalidity or non-acceptance of the prayer without the stated requirement
key_terms.مُسْتَعْجِلًا: being hurried or pressed for time

ai.seo_question: Is reciting Fatihat al-Kitab obligatory in salat, even when one is afraid or in a hurry?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the recitation of Fatihat al-Kitab is necessary in salat, whether the prayer is recited aloud or silently. It also indicates that in a state of fear or haste, reciting Fatihat al-Kitab takes priority over reciting an additional surah.
